roleZh: 布莱切利园最早的破译者 · 「迪利的姑娘们」的导师
roleEn: Bletchley Park's original codebreaker · mentor of "Dilly's girls"
bioZh: 迪利·诺克斯是英国古典学学者与密码学家。一战时他效力于海军部40号房间，破译德国海军密码。1937 年，他用自创的「钓竿」(rodding) 法——以金属杆模拟转子接线——破解了意大利海军 Enigma，为 1941 年马塔潘角海战的关键情报奠定基础。1941 年 12 月，他带领「迪利的姑娘们」首次破译德方军事情报机构 Abwehr 的 Enigma，让盟军得以监视整个德国间谍网。他 1943 年因癌症去世，功绩多年后才为世人所知。
bioEn: Dilly Knox was an English classical scholar turned cryptanalyst, and one of Bletchley Park's first codebreakers. Recruited into Room 40 during the First World War, he cut his teeth breaking German naval codes. In 1937 he cracked the Italian Navy's Enigma, devising his celebrated "rodding" method — metal rods that simulated the rotor wirings — an achievement that underpinned vital intelligence for the Battle of Cape Matapan in 1941. His greatest triumph came in December 1941, when he and his "Dilly's girls" (Mavis Lever and Margaret Rock) broke the Abwehr's Enigma, exposing the entire German military-intelligence spy network. Knox died of cancer in 1943; his work stayed classified for decades.
quoteZh: 机器的秘密，最终总是被人的习惯出卖。
quoteEn: In the end, it is always human habit that betrays the machine.
factZh: 冷知识：破译 Abwehr Enigma 的关键线索，是德方密文几乎都以「ATTENTION」开头——玛维斯·利弗发现这个固定格式后，等于把一段明文直接送进了迪利团队的破译流程。
factEn: Fun fact: the Abwehr Enigma fell partly because German messages so often began "ATTENTION" — Mavis Lever spotted the giveaway, handing Dilly's team a chunk of free plaintext.

roleZh: 国际象棋大师 · Hut 8 破译 Enigma 的核心数学家
roleEn: British chess champion · the mathematician who led Hut 8
bioZh: 休·亚历山大是英国国际象棋大师与数学家。1938 年他夺得英国国际象棋冠军，同年进入布莱切利园，加入图灵的 Hut 8 小组，参与攻克最难啃的德国海军 Enigma——1941 年 5 月击沉俾斯麦号所依赖的破译情报，就出自他所在团队的成果。图灵 1942 年赴美后，他接任 Hut 8 负责人直至战争结束。战后他投身计算机行业，先后任职于约翰·刘易斯百货与英国电气公司，成为英国计算机产业的先驱。
bioEn: Hugh Alexander was an Irish-born British chess master and mathematician. He won the British Chess Championship in 1938, the same year he was recruited to Bletchley Park. In Alan Turing's Hut 8 he tackled the hardest target of all — German naval Enigma — and the section's breakthroughs helped sink the battleship Bismarck in May 1941. When Turing left for the United States in 1942, Alexander took over as head of Hut 8 and led it until the war's end. Afterward he carried computing into British industry, working for the John Lewis Partnership and English Electric, and became a pioneer of the nation's computer industry.
quoteZh: 破译海军 Enigma 就像下棋：先弄清机器的走法，再算尽它所有的变化。
quoteEn: Breaking naval Enigma was like chess: learn how the machine moves, then count every one of its variations.
factZh: 冷知识：亚历山大战后仍是英格兰棋坛的顶梁柱——他曾多次代表英国出战国际象棋奥林匹克赛，还著有研究棋王阿廖欣的名作，是少有的以密码学家与棋手双重身份名留青史的人物。
factEn: Fun fact: Alexander stayed a force in chess for life — he represented England at the Chess Olympiads and wrote a celebrated study of Alekhine, carving his name into both cryptology and chess history.

roleZh: 「美国密码学第一夫人」· 走私犯与纳粹间谍的克星
roleEn: "First lady of American cryptology" · breaker of smugglers and Nazi spies
bioZh: 伊丽莎白·弗里德曼是美国密码学家，威廉·弗里德曼之妻，人称「美国密码学第一夫人」。一战时她成为美国首批女性密码破译员，率先把统计学方法系统引入密码分析。1930 年代禁酒令时期，她为美国海岸警卫队与财政部破译数千份走私犯密电，把贩酒集团头目一一送上法庭；二战中她识破盘踞南美的纳粹间谍网，还破获了著名的「娃娃女人」间谍案。晚年她与丈夫合著《莎士比亚密码》，用统计方法检验莎剧署名之谜。
bioEn: Elizebeth Friedman was an American cryptanalyst — wife of William Friedman — and is remembered as the "first lady of American cryptology." During the First World War she became one of America's first female codebreakers and an early champion of statistical methods. In the Prohibition era she broke thousands of messages for the Coast Guard and Treasury, sending rum-running gang leaders to prison; in the Second World War she unmasked Nazi spy rings in South America, including the notorious "Doll Woman" case. In retirement she and her husband wrote The Shakespearean Ciphers Examined, applying statistics to claims of hidden messages in the plays.
quoteZh: 每一份密报都是一句谎言，而统计数字会说出真话。
quoteEn: Every coded message is a lie — but the statistics always tell the truth.
factZh: 冷知识：她的名字 Elizebeth 刻意少用一个字母（拼作 -ze- 而非 -za-），只为与常见的 Elizabeth 区分——可直到今天，她的墓碑与纪念文字仍时常被人拼错。
factEn: Fun fact: her name "Elizebeth" was deliberately spelled with an unusual -ze- to set it apart from the common Elizabeth — yet even her tombstone and modern tributes still get it wrong.

roleZh: 多表替换密码的集大成者 · 「维吉尼亚密码」的命名者
roleEn: Master of polyalphabetic ciphers · the name behind the "Vigenère cipher"
bioZh: 布莱斯·德·维吉尼亚是法国外交官与密码学家。他出身外交世家，青年时出使罗马，在教廷钻研大量密码文献。1586 年，他出版《密码论》，系统整理并推广多表替换思想，还独创了「自动密钥」密码——让明文字母自身延伸为密钥。虽然这套方案的核心思想源自意大利人贝拉索，19 世纪起它却被冠以维吉尼亚之名，成为西方密码史上最著名的「不可破译的密码」，直到 1863 年才被卡西斯基攻破。
bioEn: Blaise de Vigenère was a French diplomat and cryptographer. Born into a diplomatic family, he served on missions to Rome, where he studied the cipher literature of the papal court. In 1586 he published Traicté des chiffres, a comprehensive treatise that popularised polyalphabetic substitution and introduced his own invention, the autokey cipher, in which the plaintext itself extends the key. Though the core scheme had actually been devised by the Italian Bellaso decades earlier, 19th-century writers attached Vigenère's name to it — and the "Vigenère cipher" became the most celebrated "indecipherable cipher" of the Western world until Kasiski broke it in 1863.
quoteZh: 让字母表转动起来，频率分析就失去了立足之地。
quoteEn: Rotate the alphabet, and frequency analysis loses its footing.
factZh: 冷知识：维吉尼亚晚年痴迷炼金术与神秘学，《密码论》出版时他已年过六旬——密码学只是这位外交官多彩人生的晚年一章，却成了他身后最响亮的名字。
factEn: Fun fact: Vigenère wrote his famous treatise in his sixties, after a long life as diplomat and alchemist — cryptography was a late hobby, yet it made his name immortal.

roleZh: 公钥密码学奠基人 · Diffie-Hellman 密钥交换提出者
roleEn: Founder of public-key cryptography · co-inventor of the Diffie–Hellman key exchange
bioZh: 马丁·赫尔曼是美国密码学家、斯坦福大学教授。1976 年，他与惠特菲尔德·迪菲发表划时代论文《密码学的新方向》，提出 Diffie-Hellman 密钥交换：双方在公开信道上即可协商出共享密钥，无需任何事先的秘密约定。这篇论文宣告公钥密码学的诞生，直接启发了 RSA 等后续体制，他本人也于 2015 年与迪菲同获图灵奖。晚年的他把目光转向核风险与全球安全，认为「和平」与密码学一样值得精心守护。
bioEn: Martin Hellman is an American cryptographer and Stanford professor. In 1976, with Whitfield Diffie, he published "New Directions in Cryptography," proposing the Diffie–Hellman key exchange: two parties negotiate a shared secret over a public channel, with no prior secret meeting. The paper gave birth to public-key cryptography and inspired the RSA system that followed; its scheme remains the basis of secure key exchange on the internet today. For this work he and Diffie shared the 2015 Turing Award. In later life Hellman turned to nuclear-risk analysis and global security, arguing, together with his wife Dorothie, that peace deserves the same careful engineering as cryptography.
quoteZh: 密码学证明了一件事：陌生人之间，也能共享一个只有彼此知道的秘密。
quoteEn: Cryptography proved that even strangers can share a secret known only to the two of them.
factZh: 冷知识：1975 年，美国国家安全局曾施压要求撤回迪菲-赫尔曼的论文，就此拉开「密码战争」的序幕——可论文最终还是照常发表，公钥密码也随之传遍世界。
factEn: Fun fact: in 1975 the NSA pressed to have Diffie and Hellman's work suppressed — the opening shot of the "Crypto Wars." The paper was published anyway, and public-key cryptography swept the world.
